vulnerabilities.name: XXE via Python XML Parsers With Untrusted Input
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted XML is parsed by a Python XML library configured to resolve DTDs or external entities, so a crafted DOCTYPE can make the server read local files or issue network requests.
vulnerabilities.notes: Python's standard xml.etree.ElementTree does not resolve external entities by default, but lxml with resolve_entities=True or load_dtd=True does. Recommend defusedxml. Flag when untrusted data reaches a parser with unsafe options.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE via Java XML Parsers Without Secure Processing
vulnerabilities.description: A Java DocumentBuilderFactory, SAXParserFactory, XMLInputFactory, TransformerFactory, SchemaFactory, or XMLReader processes untrusted XML without disabling DOCTYPE declarations or external entity resolution.
vulnerabilities.notes: Not a finding if the factory sets disallow-doctype-decl=true, or disables external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities, or enables FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING together with the accessExternalDTD/accessExternalSchema restrictions. Check for these calls near the sink.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE via PHP libxml/SimpleXML/DOM Parsing
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted XML is parsed by SimpleXML, DOMDocument, or XMLReader with LIBXML_NOENT or LIBXML_DTDLOAD, or on a PHP/libxml combination where entity substitution is enabled.
vulnerabilities.notes: libxml2 >= 2.9 does not substitute entities by default, so the main risk comes from explicit LIBXML_NOENT/LIBXML_DTDLOAD flags or very old environments.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE via .NET XmlDocument/XmlTextReader/XmlReader Misconfiguration
vulnerabilities.description: A .NET XML parser is used on untrusted input with DtdProcessing set to Parse or a non-null XmlResolver, which allows external entity resolution.
vulnerabilities.notes: Modern .NET (4.5.2+) defaults to a null resolver for most readers. Confirm explicit unsafe settings or legacy target frameworks.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE via Node.js/Ruby XML Libraries With Entity Substitution
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted XML is parsed by libxmljs, node-xml2js-based wrappers, or Ruby's Nokogiri/REXML with entity substitution or DTD loading enabled.
vulnerabilities.notes: Flag primarily when noent/NOENT/DTDLOAD options are explicitly set on untrusted input. REXML is vulnerable to entity-expansion DoS even when external entities are not resolved.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE Behavioral Indicator: Local File Content Reflected in Response
vulnerabilities.description: After a benign external-entity test is sent in an XML body, the response contains the content of a well-known local file, which proves the server resolved the external entity and returned its contents.

reflection_indicators.root:[x*]:0:0:: first field of a Unix /etc/passwd entry appears in the response
reflection_indicators.\\[(fonts|extensions|mci extensions)\\]: section header of the Windows win.ini file appears in the response
reflection_indicators.\\[boot loader\\]: section header of the legacy Windows boot.ini file appears in the response
reflection_indicators.daemon:[x*]:\\d+:\\d+:: second /etc/passwd entry pattern appears in the response

vulnerabilities.notes: Confirm with a control request that has no DOCTYPE and verify that the file markers appear only when the entity reference is present. For blind XXE, use a unique out-of-band callback hostname instead.

vulnerabilities.name: XML Parser Error Message Disclosure
vulnerabilities.description: Malformed XML or DOCTYPE content triggers a verbose parser error in the response. It confirms that user input reaches an XML parser, may reveal file paths, and shows whether DTD processing is allowed or blocked.

reflection_indicators.DOCTYPE is disallowed when the feature \: Java parser with DOCTYPE blocked (good hardening signal, but confirms an XML parser)
reflection_indicators.XML Parsing Error|This page contains the: Browser or server XML parse error page

vulnerabilities.notes: Messages such as 'Failed to load external entity' strongly suggest that entity resolution is attempted and warrant a deeper XXE test. 'DOCTYPE is disallowed' indicates hardening.

vulnerabilities.name: XML Entity Expansion (Billion Laughs / Quadratic Blowup) Exposure
vulnerabilities.description: The XML parser expands nested or repeated internal entities without limits on expansion depth, size, or count, so a small document can consume excessive memory and CPU.
vulnerabilities.notes: Test safely with a small, bounded entity-expansion document and measure response time and size. Do not send high-amplification payloads to production systems.

vulnerabilities.name: XInclude Processing Enabled on Untrusted XML
vulnerabilities.description: The parser has XInclude processing enabled, so an attacker who controls only part of the document (and cannot add a DOCTYPE) can still include local or remote resources.
vulnerabilities.notes: Relevant when user input is embedded into a server-side XML document (for example SOAP wrappers) rather than being the whole document.

vulnerabilities.name: XPath Injection via Concatenated Query Strings
vulnerabilities.description: User input is concatenated or formatted into an XPath expression, letting an attacker alter the query logic to bypass authentication or extract arbitrary nodes from the XML data store.
vulnerabilities.notes: Confirmed when a source flows into the XPath string without parameterization (XPathVariableResolver, bound variables) or strict quote escaping. Sending a single quote and observing a parse error or changed result set is a common behavioral confirmation.

vulnerabilities.name: XPath Injection Error Indicator in Response
vulnerabilities.description: A stray quote or bracket in a parameter causes the server to return an XPath syntax or evaluation error, which indicates that the input is placed inside an XPath expression.
vulnerabilities.notes: Pair this with the source-code rule above, or confirm with a boolean-differential test (two inputs that should produce different true/false outcomes).

vulnerabilities.name: XSLT Injection / Unsafe Stylesheet Processing
vulnerabilities.description: Untrusted data controls an XSLT stylesheet (or its parameters/URL) that is processed server-side. Depending on the processor and its features, this can lead to file read, SSRF, or code execution through extension functions.
vulnerabilities.notes: Flag when the stylesheet source, stylesheet URL, or an XSLT parameter is attacker-influenced. Processors with document(), script blocks, or Java/PHP extension functions are the highest risk.

vulnerabilities.name: XML Accepted Where JSON Expected (Content-Type Switching Exposure)
vulnerabilities.description: An endpoint that normally accepts JSON also accepts and parses application/xml or text/xml bodies, exposing a hidden XML parser to XXE and entity-expansion attacks.

reflection_indicators.<\\?xml\\s+version=: response returned as XML after the request Content-Type was switched from JSON
reflection_indicators.<(error|fault|response|result)\\b[^>]*>: XML-formatted error or result element returned for an XML request

vulnerabilities.notes: Resend a known-good JSON request converted to equivalent XML with the Content-Type header changed. If the request is processed, test the endpoint for XXE.

vulnerabilities.name: XXE via File Upload (SVG/DOCX/XLSX/XML Documents)
vulnerabilities.description: The application parses uploaded SVG, Office Open XML (docx/xlsx/pptx), GPX, RSS, or generic XML files server-side (thumbnailing, preview, import, metadata extraction) with an XML parser that resolves external entities.
vulnerabilities.notes: Parsers inside document libraries are frequent XXE sources because they are rarely hardened by the application developer. Keep libraries patched and verify their XML hardening defaults.

vulnerabilities.name: SOAP/XML-RPC Endpoint Exposing Verbose XML Processing
vulnerabilities.description: A SOAP, WS-*, or XML-RPC endpoint accepts raw XML requests and returns detailed faults, which makes it a primary target for XXE, XPath, and entity-expansion testing.

reflection_indicators.<soap(env)?:Envelope|<s:Envelope|<SOAP-E: SOAP envelope returned in the response
reflection_indicators.<faultstring>[^<]*(Exception|at [\\w.$]+: SOAP fault containing a stack trace or exception class

vulnerabilities.notes: Treat as an attack-surface finding. Combine with XXE and error-disclosure rules to assess exploitability. Disable verbose faults and WSDL exposure in production when not needed.
